facts.text: Wheeled machines roll on rubber tires, while tracked or crawler machines run on steel or rubber belts; the two types grip, steer and stop differently.
facts.quote: Wheeled machines roll on rubber tires, tracked or crawler machines run on steel or rubber belts, and the two grip, steer and stop differently.

facts.text: Wheel loaders, haul trucks and articulated haulers run on large tires, whereas dozers, most excavators and some loaders run on tracks.
facts.quote: A wheel loader, haul truck or articulated hauler runs on large tires; a dozer, most excavators and some loaders run on tracks

facts.text: Tracks spread machine weight over a large footprint, sink less in soft ground and retain more grip in mud; crawlers are used for heavy pushing but are slow.
facts.quote: Tracks sink less in soft ground and keep more grip in mud, which is why crawlers do the heavy pushing, but they are slow.

facts.text: ISO 3450 covers wheeled and fast rubber-tracked machines, while ISO 10265 covers crawlers at 20 km/h or less; the brake standards distinguish the categories at 20 km/h.
facts.quote: The brake standards draw the line at 20 km/h: ISO 3450 covers wheeled and fast rubber-tracked machines, ISO 10265 covers crawlers at 20 km/h or less [Chapter 8].

facts.text: For wheeled machines, the booklet identifies wheel slip, the load on each wheel, and forward and sideways tire forces as essential quantities.
facts.quote: For a wheeled machine the booklet says the essential quantities are wheel slip, the load on each wheel and the forward and sideways tire forces.

facts.text: For crawlers, force is spread along a long contact patch; relevant quantities and motions include sinkage, soil shearing by grousers, differential track speed, skid steering and counter-rotation.
facts.quote: sinkage, the shearing of soil by the grousers (the ridges on the track plates), differential track speed, skid steering (one track faster than the other) and counter-rotation (tracks turning in opposite directions to spin the machine in place) all matter [Chapter 8].

facts.text: A crawler can collide while turning on the spot even with no forward speed.
facts.quote: A crawler can therefore collide while turning on the spot with no forward speed at all

facts.text: The forthcoming standard ISO/PRF 21815-5 identifies differential speed, skid turning and counter rotation as collision-relevant motions.
facts.quote: the forthcoming standard ISO/PRF 21815-5 names differential speed, skid turning and counter rotation as collision-relevant motions [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet uses wheeled versus crawler as the first discriminator for dividing the product range into machine families with separate braking models, because their physics, brake standards and test methods differ.
facts.quote: Wheeled versus crawler is the first discriminator the booklet uses to divide the product range into machine families with separate braking models, because the physics, the brake standard and the test methods all differ [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The fastest brake-response figure quoted in the booklet is under 0.3 s for a tracked vehicle's electro-hydraulic brake, measured on one machine.
facts.quote: The fastest brake-response figure the booklet quotes, under 0.3 s, is for a tracked vehicle's electro-hydraulic brake, measured on one machine [Chapter 8].
